grade.first_issue: The inference that continuity of a on S=Im(f), together with constancy on each connected component of S, makes a locally constant on S is false: connected components of an arbitrary subset of R need not be relatively open.
grade.summary: The candidate family is verified correctly, and the proof validly derives f(f(y))=2f(y)-y, invariance a(f(y))=a(y), nonnegativity of a, and useful quadratic comparison bounds. However, the sole argument establishing global constancy of a rests on a false topological inference. It neither proves that different components of Im(f) have the same defect value nor excludes coexistence of zero and positive defect values. Those are the central difficulties of the problem and require substantial orbit-comparison and separation arguments. Thus the correct final classification is not proved as submitted.
strengths: Correctly verifies every function f(x)=x+C with C>=0.
Correctly obtains the iterate formula f^(n)(y)=y+n a(y) and hence a(y)>=0.
Correctly derives two-sided estimates comparing a(x) with a(z) for z in Im(f).

errors.description: Continuity on Im(f) and constancy on its connected components do not imply local constancy there; the components may accumulate and need not be open.

Even local constancy of a on Im(f) would not, merely from a(x)=a(f(x)), imply local constancy on the whole domain without continuity or another control on f. Consequently the decisive conclusion that a is globally constant is unsupported.
